The company's ADMT use — or its use of personal information to train an ADMT — may have begun before these regulations took effect and still be ongoing. If so, there is a firm outer deadline for coming into compliance with the Article 10 risk-assessment duty that use triggers. The CPPA explained in its Final Statement of Reasons that it set that deadline because it wanted businesses to know precisely when they must be in compliance: "The Agency chose December 31, 2027, as the calendar deadline" — roughly 24 months after the regulations were approved. That is separate from the January 1, 2027 deadline for the ADMT notice, opt-out, and access duties this report otherwise addresses (11 CCR § 7200(b)); the risk-assessment deadline runs on its own clock. Whether this company's ADMT use is inside or outside that window, and whether a risk assessment has been completed for it, are questions about this company's own timeline, not this citation. (California Privacy Protection Agency, Final Statement of Reasons, CCPA Updates, Cyber, Risk, ADMT, and Insurance Regulations, 11 CCR § 7155(c), p. 39.)
